gaps.sentence: ___ of my two brothers work in banking.
gaps.explanation: 'Both of my two brothers work ...' is correct; 'all' and 'none' are not used for two.

gaps.hint: general statement without 'the' — 'people' has no article
gaps.explanation: 'Most people' means people in general; 'most of' needs 'the' (most of the people).

gaps.sentence: The ___ of teenagers own a smartphone these days.
gaps.explanation: 'The majority of + plural noun' means most of them; 'the number of teenagers own' would be ungrammatical.

gaps.sentence: This cup is cracked — could I have ___ one?
gaps.explanation: 'Another one' means one more, unspecified; 'the other one' would mean a specific second cup.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ patience with rude customers.
This year the festival attracted ___ visitors than in 2024.
gaps.explanation: 'Fewer' is the comparative for countable plurals like visitors; 'less' is for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: There isn't ___ room for another desk in here.
___ of the workforce is part-time now.
gaps.hint: pattern: ___ of + specific group; singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Half of the workforce is ...' is the correct pattern; 'the half of' is not used in this position.
